# Read-Back

One baker is making two 900 g country loaves from a single batch of dough, using one oven and one Dutch oven (which must bake the loaves sequentially because there is only one). The process starts at 8 a.m. The levain is prepared first and must dome and smell sweet over 4–6 hours at room temperature. The dough is mixed at 8:30 a.m., autolysed for 1 hour, then mixed with the ripe levain and salt, folded three times at half-hour intervals during a 3–5 hour bulk fermentation. The shaped boules are retarded in the refrigerator for 10–14 hours overnight. The next day, the Dutch oven is preheated 45 minutes before the dough comes out of the fridge; the first loaf is scored, baked covered for 20 minutes and uncovered for 20 more, then cooled for at least 1 hour; the Dutch oven is reheated for 10 minutes; the second loaf is scored and baked the same way (40 minutes total), then cooled on the rack beside the first. The sole constraint is that one oven, one Dutch oven, and one refrigerator serve the whole process, and the two loaves must bake one after the other because there is only one Dutch oven. No explicit finish deadline is given; the work finishes when the second loaf is cool.
